The Week Guide

This Week in the Bay

Tuesday 25 – Sunday 30 August 2026

The moon goes 96 percent dark over the Bay on Thursday night, and three museums have built their evening around it. Elsewhere: a 176-speaker theatre plays its last night in total darkness, a five-day thinking festival takes over a stretch of Telegraph Avenue, Harold Lloyd hangs off a clock face to a live orchestra, and a noise show serves pancakes at noon. Midweek is attached — which is where the talks, the piano festival and every museum after-hours night actually live.

Thu 27 Aug — 96% partial lunar eclipse, max 9:13pm Clear skies Thu–Sat — telescope nights are on SF International Piano Festival, all week Free Saturday at the de Young & Legion Shotgun's Iphigenia closes Sat Audium's Hidden Currents closes Sat

Top 5 This Week

If you only do five things. Thursday is the busiest night of the week by a wide margin — the eclipse pulls everything into it.

  1. After Dark: Deep Observations — Exploratorium
    Thu Aug 27, 6–10pm · Pier 15, Embarcadero · 18+ · ~$25–40
    The single best-assembled night of the week. A physicist on gravitational-wave detection scored live for Ben Goldberg's clarinet, James Allister Sprang's 17-instrument spatial-audio piece in the Kanbar Forum, sensory installations built around slow attention — and, on the pier outside, the SF Amateur Astronomers with telescopes trained on a 96-percent lunar eclipse.
  2. Audium: Hidden Currents by golden lionheart collier — closing weekend
    Thu 27, Fri 28, Sat 29 Aug · 8pm (doors 7:30) · 1616 Bush St, Lower Nob Hill · $22.75–33
    176 speakers, total darkness, no stage. collier moves hundreds of field recordings — Candomblé devotees, a New Orleans second line, bomba, ring shouts, water drumming, Hoodoo elders — through the room to trace Maafa migration routes. Friday adds a post-show Q&A with the artist; Saturday is the last night of the run.
  3. Bathers Library Summer Symposium (2nd annual)
    Wed Aug 26 – Sun Aug 30 · 2310 Telegraph Ave, Uptown Oakland + satellites · $60–120 pass, NOTAFLOF
    Five days of the Oakland artist-run scene thinking out loud: a brief history of reverb, Gertrude Stein and nonsense, the poetry and philosophy of Oakland code enforcement, culinary taboos from pork to sago grubs, Adrian Daub reading from What Tech Calls Governing. It ends Sunday with a sauna. Single-day passes at the door.
  4. The Soiled Dove — Vau de Vire Society, with Joan Baez
    Fri 28 & Sat 29 Aug · dinner doors 7:30pm, main show 9pm · The Big Top, Radium Runway, Alameda · $75–214 · 21+
    A 12,000-square-foot Italian circus tent on a seaplane lagoon, an entirely new Barbary Coast story this season, aerial and cabaret acts over a three-course dinner — and Joan Baez joining the cast in a new role. Chronicle Datebook and KQED both wrote it up. Period costume strongly encouraged.
  5. Safety Last! (1923) — live orchestra + Wurlitzer concert
    Wed Aug 26 · organ concert 6pm, film 7pm · Grand Lake Theatre, Oakland · $45 / $40 senior / $15 child
    Harold Lloyd dangling off the clock face, with a full orchestra in a 1926 movie palace and the house Wurlitzer warmed up for an hour beforehand. Billed "One Night Only — JUST ADDED." The Grand Lake is also running Nolan's Odyssey on genuine 70mm all week.

Oddities & One-Offs

The small, strange and only-this-week. An eclipse, a noon noise matinee with pancakes, and a cathedral playing its own silent bells.

TOP PICK✦ Once this year

Partial Lunar Eclipse Watch Party

Thu Aug 27 · 7–10pm (max eclipse 9:13pm)

Chabot Space & Science Center, Oakland Hills East Bay

96 percent of the moon slides into Earth's shadow — a partial eclipse deep enough to read as total. Live commentary in Studio 3, then out to the observation deck and the historic refractors. Fog backup is a livestream in the 70-foot planetarium dome. The only deep lunar eclipse visible from the Bay this year.

$24 adults · $19 kids · free for members

✦ DIY house show

G|O|D|W|A|F|F|L|E ‖ N|O|I|S|E ‖ P|A|N|C|A|K|E|S

Sat Aug 29 · 12–2pm

A house on Thornhill Dr, Oakland Hills East Bay

Twenty-six years of noon noise matinees in someone's living room, and they still make you gourmet pancakes and coffee on the way in. This edition: Tom Djll, Decision/Fatigue, Tanuki Spider Cat, Wilderman, Tone Shepherd, Shit Matrix. Six dollars "or whatever."

$6 or whatever

✦ Residency installation

Bill Fontana: Resonance

Tue 12–1pm & 2–3pm · Wed 1–3pm · Fri 12–2pm · Sat 11am–1pm

Grace Cathedral, Nob Hill San Francisco

Fontana — who did the same thing with the bells of Notre-Dame — has wired Grace's silent bells and organ pipes into a sound sculpture, so the cathedral plays an instrument that is otherwise mute. Lie down on the labyrinth and listen. Free with entry.

Free with cathedral entry

✦ Rare local club date

Fred Frith's FREMAKAJO + Jordan Glenn's BEAK

Wed Aug 26 · 7:30pm

Ivy Room, Albany East Bay

The founding figure of Bay Area avant-garde guitar, in a 150-capacity bar on San Pablo Avenue. Frith almost never plays local club dates any more. Drummer Jordan Glenn's BEAK opens.

~$20 at the door

✦ Rare US date

Merope, with Shahzad Ismaily

Fri Aug 28 · 8:30pm (doors 8pm)

The Lab, 2948 16th St, Mission San Francisco

Lithuanian kanklės-and-voice duo playing what they call celestial ambient folk, with Bert Cools on treated guitar and Shahzad Ismaily sitting in. David Wesley Golightly opens with a solo piano album release. The Lab's concrete room is the right one for it.

$23 · free or discounted for members

✦ Free, historic instruments

Free Telescope Viewings — Chabot Observatory Deck

Fri Aug 28 & Sat Aug 29 · 7:30–10:30pm

Chabot, 10000 Skyline Blvd, Oakland East Bay

Leah (8-inch, 1883) and Rachel (20-inch, 1916 — the largest refractor in the West regularly open to the public), plus the 36-inch reflector Nellie, 1,500 feet above the Bay. Costs nothing. Forecast is clear both nights, but they close on humidity, so check before you drive up.

Free

✦ Sells out

Lick Observatory After Hours

Fri Aug 28 & Sat Aug 29 · from 6pm (4–6 hrs)

Mt Hamilton, above San Jose South Bay

The 46th Summer Series: a behind-the-scenes walk of the Eastside to the Shane Telescope, a twilight history lecture on the mountain, then stargazing through portable scopes. About a mile of walking at 4,200 feet. The main building is still shut from the December storm damage.

$81.88 all-in

DOMI + Ken Ueno & Matt Ingalls — West Oakland Sound Series

Sun Aug 30 · 7:15pm

Dresher Ensemble Studio, 2201 Poplar St, Oakland East Bay

Prepared drums, scrap metal, cello, voice and salvaged resonant objects, with amplifier feedback treated as a fourth player. Then Ken Ueno's vocal multiphonics against Matt Ingalls on clarinet. Free if you're a student or underemployed.

$20 · free for students / underemployed

✦ Record release

Joseph Dee Bradshaw record release + Hi-Vis-Man ft. Bryan Day

Sat Aug 29 · 8pm

Temescal Arts Center, 511 48th St, Oakland East Bay

Bradshaw launches The Lavender Promise; Max Abner's Corsick/Pontac fills the middle with Jacob Felix Heule, Matt Ingalls and Ben Rodgers; and Bryan Day closes playing instruments he built himself. Sliding scale.

$10–20 sliding

★ CRITICS' · 7x7✦ Final week of the season

Filoli Summer Nights

Wed Aug 26 & Thu Aug 27 · 5–8pm

Filoli Historic House & Garden, Woodside South Bay

Golden hour on the estate lawn with acoustic music, food and drink, the giant "Creating Home" nest installation, and a resident troll named Rose you can climb inside. 7x7 called it "your midweek escape into golden-hour California magic." Thursday adds a 6pm guided sunset hike on trails that are otherwise closed.

From $25 members · sunset hike +$30

Mission Missives Zine Expo

Sat Aug 29 · 12–4pm

Youth Art Exchange, 1950 Mission St, Studio B San Francisco

Handmade zines, original art, prints and small-press comics from Bay Area independent publishers, plus a four-artist panel on self-publishing and keeping a practice going here. Free.

Free

✦ 44th annual

44th Annual Sand Sculpture Contest, Drakes Beach

Sat Aug 29 · register 9am, judging noon, prizes 3pm

Drakes Beach, Point Reyes National Seashore North Bay

Forty-four years of an art contest with one rule: every material has to be found on the beach that morning. Children, family and adult categories plus People's Choice. Free, and the drive out is half the point.

Free

✦ Free, nightly

Photosynthesis — nightly light show

Every night · starts ~8:20pm (30 min after sunset), loops to midnight

Conservatory of Flowers, Golden Gate Park San Francisco

A psychedelic projection mapped onto the oldest wood-and-glass conservatory in North America, with a score. No ticket, no RSVP, no queue — bring a blanket and a thermos to the JFK Promenade lawn and watch it loop.

Free

Big Museums — After Hours & On View

Thursday is the after-dark night everywhere. Two blockbusters are into their final weeks.

TOP PICK✦ Eclipse night

After Dark: Deep Observations

Thu Aug 27 · 6–10pm · 18+

Exploratorium, Pier 15, Embarcadero San Francisco

A whole night built on slow attention. Dr Desiré Whitmore on LIGO and gravitational waves, accompanied by Ben Goldberg's clarinet; James Allister Sprang's 17-instrument spatial-audio piece in the Kanbar Forum at 7:30; the OBSERVER short film; sensory installations 6:30–9:30 — and telescopes on the pier for the eclipse, 7:30–9:30.

~$25–40 · free for members

✦ Eclipse from the Living Roof

NightLife: Disco

Thu Aug 27 · 6–10pm (last entry 9pm) · 21+

Cal Academy of Sciences, Golden Gate Park San Francisco

The disco conceit is a lit-up dance floor and drag disco bingo in African Hall; the reason to go is that the SF Amateur Astronomers set up on the Living Roof for the eclipse, with the aquarium, rainforest and planetarium open around you. Food trucks in the East Garden.

$26 · +$7 planetarium · $5 with EBT

✦ Opens this Thursday

Art from Contemporary Cambodia

Opens Thu Aug 27 · Thu 1–8pm, Fri–Mon 10–5

Asian Art Museum, Civic Center San Francisco

Sopheap Pich and Leang Seckon, both Khmer Rouge survivors: Seckon's collages built from recycled textiles and photographs, Pich's abstract sculpture made from natural and discarded material. It opens inside this window, on the museum's late night.

Included with admission

Friday Nights at OMCA with BULULÚ

Fri Aug 28 · 5–9pm

Oakland Museum of California, 1000 Oak St East Bay

The reliable one: eleven Off the Grid trucks along 10th Street, late galleries, bars in the garden. This week it's BULULÚ, a Caribbean ensemble led by Venezuelan percussionist Lali Mejia, plus an Afro dance lesson with Danaite Gebremeskel. Grounds are free.

Free (galleries need admission)

★ CRITICS' · Mission Local✦ One performance

Paris Portraits — staged reading

Thu Aug 27 · 6pm

SFMOMA, Phyllis Wattis Theater, SoMa San Francisco

Harriet Lane Levy sailed for Paris in 1907 with Alice B. Toklas and wrote down what she saw: the Stein salons, the Picasso–Matisse rivalry, Montmartre, a single woman abroad. Laura Sheppard performs it with Dale Tsang at the piano, timed to the Matisse show upstairs. Pay what you wish.

Free RSVP / $10 / $20 / $30

★ CRITICS' · Mission Local + 7x7✦ Final weeks

The Etruscans: From the Heart of Ancient Italy

Tue–Sun 9:30am–5:15pm · closes Sep 20

Legion of Honor, Lincoln Park San Francisco

The largest US showing of Etruscan material — 150 sculptures and jewels from a civilisation we mostly know through its tombs. Mission Local: "so many good word-of-mouth reviews... it sounds like a must." Free guided tours daily at 12:30, and free entry Saturday for nine-county residents.

Admission + exhibition ticket · free Sat for Bay Area residents

★ CRITICS' · Mission Local

Treasures of the Pharaohs

Tue–Sun 9:30am–5:15pm

de Young, Golden Gate Park San Francisco

Gilded coffins, gold masks and royal jewellery on loan from Egypt — the blockbuster of the year. Mission Local's review: "not only culturally and financially valuable, they are also visually stunning." Saturday Aug 29 is free for Bay Area residents, which is the way to do it.

Exhibition ticket · free Sat for Bay Area residents

★ CRITICS' · Mission Local✦ Free, no ticket

Jacob Hashimoto: Giant Arc

Mon/Tue/Fri–Sun 10–5, Thu 12–8 · closed Wed

SFMOMA, Roberts Family Gallery, SoMa San Francisco

Roughly 75,000 hand-built bamboo-and-paper kites massed into a floor-to-ceiling canopy — the largest work of Hashimoto's career, and it hangs in the one SFMOMA gallery that sits outside the ticket barrier. Walk in off Third Street for nothing.

Free

✦ Closes Sep 13

Matisse's Femme au chapeau: A Modern Scandal

Mon/Tue/Fri–Sun 10–5, Thu 12–8 · closed Wed

SFMOMA Floor 4, SoMa San Francisco

A whole show built around one painting — the Fauve scandal picture the Steins bought in 1905 and carried into the salons that Paris Portraits is about. Doing the reading and the show in one visit is the move this week.

$30 + surcharge

Mildred Howard: Poetics of Memory

Wed–Sun 11am–5pm (Fri to 9pm) · through Oct 18

Oakland Museum of California, Great Hall East Bay

The first major museum survey for the Berkeley assemblage artist — five decades of collage, found-object sculpture and immersive installation, including work pulled straight out of her studio that has never been shown. The flagship East Bay exhibition right now.

Included with admission

Mahjong and Mocktails

Thu Aug 27 · from 5pm (museum open till 8)

Asian Art Museum, 200 Larkin St, Civic Center San Francisco

Tiles and instructors provided, no experience assumed, drinks alongside — and the Cambodia show opens the same evening upstairs. The low-effort version of a Thursday night out.

Included with general admission

Motherboards

Through Jan 10, 2027 · free Thu 6–9pm

San José Museum of Art, 110 S Market St South Bay

Women's labour as the actual substrate of the tech industry — looms, assembly lines, Silicon Valley garages, the hands that wound the wire. The best art show in the South Bay right now, and free on Thursday evening.

Ticketed · free Thu 6–9pm

Contemporary Painting in Papua New Guinea: Mathias Kauage and His Family

Tue–Sun 9:30am–5:15pm · through Dec 6

de Young, Golden Gate Park San Francisco

A painting dynasty almost never shown in the US — vivid, flat, deeply strange work from a family that made modern PNG art out of contact-era subject matter. The sleeper in the building while everyone queues for the pharaohs.

Included with admission

Galleries & Artist Spaces

Late August is the SF gallery dead zone — and then Saturday the 29th detonates: four openings and two artist talks in one afternoon.

TOP PICK✦ Artist remarks at 3pm

Sandow Birk: An Illustrated History of the Present — opening

Sat Aug 29 · 2–4pm (remarks 3pm)

Catharine Clark Gallery, 248 Utah St, Potrero San Francisco

Three decades of Birk in one room — the Depravities of War woodcuts, the American Qur'an, the whole satirical-history project by an artist who paints the present as if it were already a chapter heading. Opens Catharine Clark's 35th-anniversary year, with Birk speaking at three.

Free

✦ Opening night

Table Manners — opening reception

Sat Aug 29 · 5–7pm

Hashimoto Contemporary, Minnesota Street Project, Dogpatch San Francisco

Twenty-four painters on food — the shared meal, the leftovers, what we attach to it. Mary Finlayson, Stacey Rozich, Zoe Hawk, Monika Marchewka, Adrian Kay Wong. Three hours after Birk, ten minutes away, and the same building holds the Asawa show.

Free

✦ Unusual format · 17th annual

FourSquared XVII — opening reception

Sat Aug 29 · 7–9pm

Arc Studios & Gallery, 1246 Folsom St, SoMa San Francisco

Sixteen Bay Area artists, sixteen small works each, hung in sixteen clusters — so the room reads as sixteen micro solo shows at once. Everything under $800. Seventeen years of this format and it still holds up. The natural third stop of the Saturday crawl.

Free

✦ Opening reception

Mitch Iburg: Talus — opening

Fri Aug 28 · 5–7pm

Hugomento, 795 22nd St, Dogpatch San Francisco

Iburg digs his own clay. This is his fourth solo here: sculpture answering the fractured limestone of Mississippi River bluffs, plus paintings made from crushed ceramic shards, unfired kaolin and glacial debris on wood. Geologic, quiet, and exactly the small-room register this lane is for.

Free · RSVP

✦ One night, tiny room

El Mad Mex Talks Back — Guillermo Gómez-Peña solo

Thu Aug 27 · 7:30–8:30pm

Adobe Books, 3130 24th St, Mission San Francisco

The La Pocha Nostra founder and MacArthur fellow performing from his "living archive" in a Mission bookshop, with poet Yates Cessna. A major performance artist in a room that holds maybe fifty people, for a fifteen-dollar donation.

$15–20 donation

✦ One night only

BYOB (Bring Your Own Beamer)

Thu Aug 27 · 7–10pm

Gray Area, 2665 Mission St San Francisco

Artists haul in their own projectors and fill the Grand Theater with whatever they've got — "hypnotic loops and generative systems to strange hardware contraptions and happy accidents." A format invented by Rafaël Rozendaal; this is the summer euphoria edition. Exists for one evening.

See event page

✦ Artist + BAMPFA chief curator

Terri Friedman: Overmuch — artist talk

Wed Aug 26 · 6–8pm

Anthony Meier, 21 Throckmorton Ave, Mill Valley North Bay

Friedman's first solo at the gallery — a decade of woven work treated as spatial intervention and emotional register, including Standing Ovation: for anyone who has had Chemotherapy. In conversation with BAMPFA chief curator Margot Norton. Free and no RSVP, which is unusual for a talk at this level.

Free · no RSVP

✦ Closing week

Tricia Rainwater in conversation with Larissa Nez

Thu Aug 27 · 6–8pm

SFAC Galleries, 401 Van Ness Ave, Civic Center San Francisco

The Choctaw multimedia artist with curator Larissa Nez on art as a healing route through femme Indigenous space. The exhibition I split the ground, so it would not close over me comes down two days later, so this is the last real chance at it.

Free

✦ Artist present

Monika Mayer: LINKED — artist talk

Sat Aug 29 · 3–5pm

Mercury 20 Gallery, 475 25th St, Uptown Oakland East Bay

Mayer takes soccer balls and inner tubes apart and zip-ties them back into organism-like clusters, alongside canvases layered in coffee, paint and ink — all keyed to the California coastline and its tides. Rainey Straus talks about her fungal, slime-mould-inspired work in the same room half an hour later.

Free

✦ Last day

Surface Tension — closing reception

Sat Aug 29 · 4–7pm

Gray Loft Gallery, 2889 Ford St, Jingletown, Oakland East Bay

Twenty photographers and painters on water, light and edge — Mark Citret, Preston Gannaway, Josie Iselin, Monica Denevan, Sally Weber. A top-floor loft in Jingletown on the last afternoon of the show.

Free

Ruth Asawa: Endless Variations

Gallery hours · through Oct 3

Ruth Asawa Lanier Inc, 1275 Minnesota St, Dogpatch San Francisco

Thirty-five years of Asawa returning to a single desert-plant motif across wire, paper, plaster, metallic foil, tin and fabric. In the same building as Saturday's Hashimoto opening, so you get both for one trip.

Free

★ CRITICS' · Mission Local

Andy Vogt: The Ringing in My Eyes + Amy Trachtenberg

Fri & Sat 12–5pm (free) · guided tour Sat 4pm

500 Capp Street — the David Ireland House, Mission San Francisco

Two installations threaded through David Ireland's house, which is itself the artwork. Mission Local: "if I were in town, I would go. 500 Capp Street is special and these installations fit right in." Self-guided is free; the Saturday tour is $20 and worth it.

Free self-guided · $20 guided tour

Classical, Opera & Jazz

The big houses are all dark until September — so the week belongs to the SF International Piano Festival, a Vatican choir, and the small rooms.

TOP PICK★ CRITICS' · SF Chronicle✦ One night, one-off ensemble

Brad Mehldau: Ride Into the Sun — the music of Elliott Smith

Sat Aug 29 · 8pm (doors 7pm)

Paramount Theatre, 2025 Broadway, Uptown Oakland East Bay

Mehldau's Elliott Smith project with Chris Thile, Blake Mills, Matt Chamberlain and John Davis, backed by the 17-piece USC Thornton Chamber Virtuosi — jazz piano, an indie songbook and a chamber orchestra in a deco movie palace. SFJAZZ presents it; it is their only event in the window, and the ensemble does not otherwise exist.

~$45–135

✦ One night · touring from Rome

Sacred Voices — singers of Rome & the Vatican

Thu Aug 27 · 8pm (seating 7:30)

Grace Cathedral, 1100 California St, Nob Hill San Francisco

Forty singers drawn from Rome's Vatican musical institutions, under Pontifical Cantor Adriano Caroletti — Palestrina, Perosi, Bartolucci, in the Sistine Chapel Choir tradition, under Grace's vaulting. One night, and the acoustic is the other half of the ticket.

$50 wings · $75 rear orchestra · $125 orchestra

✦ Festival finale

SF International Piano Festival Finale: Symphonic Dances

Sun Aug 30 · 4–6pm

Old First Church, 1751 Sacramento St, Nob Hill San Francisco

The ninth festival closes with Rachmaninoff's Symphonic Dances in the composer's own two-piano version — plus Gershwin's Cuban Overture for two pianos and Liam Teague's A Visit to Hell. Elizabeth Dorman, Jeffrey LaDeur and Karina Tseng, with the Teague steelpan duo.

$30 · $25 senior · $10 student · kids free

✦ Festival debut · unusual instrumentation

Steelpan & Piano Masterworks — Stephen Prutsman + the TNTeague Duo

Fri Aug 28 · 8pm

Old First Church, 1751 Sacramento St, Nob Hill San Francisco

Liam Teague and his son Jaden Teague-Núñez — father-and-son steelpan virtuosi — making their festival debut alongside pianist Stephen Prutsman. Steelpan-and-piano repertoire is a genuinely small shelf, and you will not hear it played at this level often.

$30 · $25 senior · $10 student

✦ Free · the Liszt B minor

Noontime Concerts: Karina Tseng, piano

Tue Aug 25 · 12:30–1:15pm

Old St Mary's Cathedral, 660 California St San Francisco

Shostakovich preludes and fugues, a Beethoven sonata, and then the whole Liszt B-minor Sonata — thirty minutes of one of the hardest things in the repertoire, on a free lunch hour, from a Bay Area native now based in Europe.

Free (donation)

✦ Three-night residency

The Coltrane Influence — Wayne Escoffery & Tal Cohen

Thu 27, Fri 28, Sat 29 Aug · two sets nightly, 7pm & ~9:15pm

Black Cat, 400 Eddy St, Tenderloin San Francisco

Escoffery (Mingus Big Band, Tom Harrell) and Israeli-Australian pianist Tal Cohen take three nights and six sets to work through what Coltrane actually left behind, from two different angles. A basement supper club is the right size for this.

$20–60 depending on seat & night

★ CRITICS' · 7x7 + SF Chronicle

Black Music Festival (5th annual)

Sun Aug 30 · 4pm (doors 3pm)

Great American Music Hall, 859 O'Farrell St San Francisco

The Dynamic Miss Faye Carol — Kehlani's mentor, and a Bay institution — leads a bill that also has Tuck & Patti and Paula West on it. Three separate Bay Area jazz and soul institutions on one stage in one afternoon, plus Rico Pabon and Tia Nomore.

$45–50

✦ Billed as a secret date

Dameron Powell

Sat Aug 29 · 5pm

Bird & Beckett, 653 Chenery St, Glen Park San Francisco

The shop is calling this a "sneak date — secret, shhhh," and then quietly lists Henry Hung, Kasey Knudsen, John Wiitala and Lorca Hart as the band. That is a serious quartet for an unannounced 5pm set.

$20 · $10 students

✦ Once a year

Annual Freight Fiddle Summit — Alasdair Fraser & Friends

Thu Aug 27 · 8pm (doors 7pm)

Freight & Salvage, 2020 Addison St, Berkeley East Bay

The Scottish master convenes every fiddler he can get on one stage, once a year, and they trade tunes until it stops. Not classical exactly, but the only night of its kind on the calendar.

$39 / $44

✦ Free · open-door masterclass

McKee Masterclass II: Stephen Prutsman

Thu Aug 27 · 3–5pm

Noe Valley Ministry, 1021 Sanchez St San Francisco

Watching a former Avery Fisher Career Grant pianist take two young players apart and put them back together is a very particular pleasure, and these are almost never open to the public. Free, but it needs a reservation. Two more run Tue and Fri.

Free · reservation required

Theater

A famous solo closes in Berkeley, a 36-year-old company premieres two plays in its final season, and seven plays written this month get one night.

TOP PICK✦ Closes Sat Aug 29

Iphigenia in Splott — Gary Owen

Wed 26 & Thu 27 7pm · Fri 28 & Sat 29 8pm — final performance Sat

Shotgun Players, The Ashby Stage, Berkeley East Bay

Alicia Mason alone on stage for a hundred minutes as a woman on a Cardiff estate who turns out to be the one paying for everyone else's austerity. James Tait Black winner, named by The Guardian one of the fifty best theatre shows of the century. The extended run ends Saturday.

$40–80 · $25 community · $15 under-25

✦ World premieres #80 & #81 · final season

The Prince, Parts 1 & 2 — Gary Graves

Thu 27, Fri 28, Sat 29 at 7pm · Sun 30 at 5pm — parts alternate; call 510.558.1381

Central Works at the Berkeley City Club East Bay

Machiavelli's life and times as a two-play cycle in a fifty-seat room in a Julia Morgan building. These are Central Works' eightieth and eighty-first world premieres — and the company, after thirty-six years, is closing. You don't need to see them in order. Currently waitlist only.

$35–45 · pay-what-you-can Thu · sliding $20–45 day-of

★ CRITICS' · Broke-Ass Stuart✦ One night, all premieres

Shotz: MAXXING — seven world-premiere short plays

Fri Aug 28 · 7–9pm

Eclectic Box, 446 Valencia St, Mission San Francisco

Seven plays written, cast, rehearsed and staged inside a single month, performed once and then gone. Scrappy by design. Five dollars gets you in; thirty is the suggested price if you can.

$5 pay-what-you-can · $30 suggested

★ CRITICS' · 48 Hills✦ Closing weekend

In Front of Your Eyes Festival — closing weekend

Thu 27 – Sun 30 Aug · evenings & matinees · closing party Sun 7pm (free)

The Marsh Berkeley, 2120 Allston Way East Bay

48 Hills: "Theatre festivals have become a rarity in the Bay Area... This is your chance to see them all first." Six works-in-progress from women and non-binary makers — Joyful Raven's Tactical Frivolity, Hannah Gould's Divorced: The Musical, Yvonne Martinez on her scab-mugging grandmother. Most shows are already waitlisted.

$15–100 sliding · closing party free

✦ Free · last Berkeley dates

WRECKAGE — SF Mime Troupe in the park

Sat Aug 29 & Sun Aug 30 · 2pm (live band 1:30)

Cedar Rose Park, Berkeley East Bay

The Tony-winning Mime Troupe's 2026 musical: a hallucinating AI at a company called Anthropomorphic, an evangelical waiting on the Rapture, a National Guardsman deployed against protesters. Brass band, blanket on the grass, free. Their last Berkeley dates before the tour moves to SF.

Free · $20 suggested

✦ Three dates left

Dan Hoyle: Takes All Kinds

Fri Aug 28 · 7:30pm

The Marsh, 1062 Valencia St, Mission San Francisco

The creator of The Real Americans back from touring: school-board showdowns in Florida, organisers in Atlanta, barbershops in Las Vegas, deprogrammers in Missouri, all played solo. Billed as a limited run — only three dates left after this.

$15–100 sliding

✦ New play

R.O.I. (Return on Investment) — Aaron Loeb

Wed 2pm & 7pm · Thu 7pm · Fri 8pm · Sat 2pm & 8pm

Creativity Theater, 221 4th St, Yerba Buena San Francisco

A VC and a visionary founder colliding over ambition, ethics and money, from SF Playhouse's resident playwright and directed by Jonathan Moscone. A new Bay Area play about the Bay Area, which is rarer than it should be.

★ CRITICS' · SF Chronicle

Much Ado About Nothing — a South Asian retelling

Select Thu–Sun at 7pm — check which nights are Much Ado vs Earnest

Silicon Valley Shakespeare, Sanborn County Park, Saratoga South Bay

Director Kunal Prasad turns the masquerade into a roka — a Hindu engagement party — and the whole comedy into a Monsoon Wedding-style celebration, played outdoors in a redwood park. It alternates in rep with The Importance of Being Earnest, so check the date.

$32–64

✦ Pay-what-you-will Thursday

Julius Caesar — dir. Jon Tracy

Thu 27 7:30pm (PWYW) · Fri 28 & Sat 29 7:30pm · Sun 30 5pm

Forest Meadows Amphitheatre, Dominican University, San Rafael North Bay

Outdoor Shakespeare on how fear, loyalty and national myth actually get made — Tracy's productions are reliably theatrical rather than reverent. Thursday is pay-what-you-will; Saturday has a post-show Kaleidoscope Talk. Bring a blanket, it gets cold.

Dance

ODC's State of Play takes over the Mission for four days with four premieres. Everything else in the lane is a one-night showcase.

TOP PICK★ CRITICS' · 7x7 + Broke-Ass Stuart✦ Four premieres

ODC Theater: State of Play 2026

Thu 27 – Sun 30 Aug · kick-off Thu 7pm, opening night Fri 7pm, six works Sat & Sun

ODC Theater & Dance Commons, 17th & Shotwell, Mission San Francisco

The contemporary dance event of the month: two West Coast premieres, a world premiere and a Bay Area premiere in four days. Passes come in Mini, Mega and Max; ODC releases free Arts Access tickets to every performance, so the real floor is zero. Thursday's kick-off is in a Jackson Square gallery.

Free–$80 · festival passes · ODC10 = 10% off 4+

✦ West Coast premiere

Leslie Cuyjet: Blur

Sat Aug 29 8:30pm · Sun Aug 30 2:30pm (ASL-interpreted)

ODC Theater, 3153 17th St, Mission San Francisco

A solo performed in a custom bodysuit printed with close-ups of her own skin — an argument about visibility, objectification, and whether she gets to control her own erasure. Sound by Brandon Wolcott; commissioned for The Shed's Open Call. Two showings only.

Free–$80

✦ West Coast premiere

Laila J. Franklin: BABYBABYBABY

Fri Aug 28 7pm (opening night + after-party) · Sat Aug 29 3:30pm

ODC Theater, Mission San Francisco

A dance about dances about love, mined out of rom-coms, dance-competition television and archival footage, by a Dance Magazine "25 to Watch" choreographer. Friday is the festival's opening night and she DJs the party afterwards.

Free–$80

✦ Bay Area premiere

LaVelle & Wiederholt: What the Hell Happened in San Francisco?

Sat Aug 29 6:30pm · Sun Aug 30 7:30pm

ODC Theater, Mission San Francisco

Two dancers who met here in 2008 make an evening-length piece about idealism and what happened to it — the most narrative, most legible thing on the festival bill, and the one most directly about this city.

Free–$80

Sharp & Fine: Talk Story

Fri 28 & Sat 29 7:30pm · Sun 30 6pm

Dance Mission Theater, 3316 24th St, Mission San Francisco

The launch of a storytelling-through-dance series: four short works by Sharp & Fine plus guests Babatunji Johnson, chinchin HSU and Molly Rose-Williams, then a casual conversation with the audience about whether dance can carry narrative at all.

Repertory Cinema

One card per film. An unusually strong week for celluloid: 16mm, an imported uncensored 35mm print, a full orchestra, and a festival projected off VHS.

Wed Aug 26 · Wurlitzer concert 6pm, film 7pm

Grand Lake Theatre, Oakland East Bay

Harold Lloyd on the clock face, with a full orchestra underneath and the house Wurlitzer given an hour of its own beforehand, in a 1926 movie palace. Billed "One Night Only! JUST ADDED."

Eyes Wide Shut (Kubrick, 1999) — 35mm

Sun Aug 30 · 7pm (159 min)

BAMPFA, 2155 Center St, Berkeley East Bay

The European cut, uncensored, on an imported 35mm archival print — a version that is essentially unavailable in the United States. Closing night of "A Complete Stanley Kubrick." If you only go to one film this week, this is the one you cannot replicate at home.

Sat Aug 29 · 3pm (137 min)

BAMPFA, Barbro Osher Theater, Berkeley East Bay

All seven parts, silent, on 16mm, as intended — Dorsky's own description is "films on a single subject, and that subject would be the light." He is in the room. Final day of the Dorsky & Hiler series.

Roxie Theater, 3117 16th St, Mission San Francisco

Maggie Cheung playing the doomed silent-era star Ruan Lingyu, in a film that keeps stopping to show you Cheung being interviewed about playing her. Kwan's masterpiece, newly restored. The best thing screening in San Francisco this week.

Jeanne Moreau walking the Champs-Élysées while Miles Davis improvises over the footage — Malle's debut, digitally restored, closing BAMPFA's French Noir series. Currently sold out; worth checking the door.

Immersive & Cabaret

A sound theatre closes, a circus tent runs two nights, and BATS gives away its fortieth birthday.

TOP PICK✦ Closing weekend

Audium: Hidden Currents — golden lionheart collier

Thu 27, Fri 28, Sat 29 Aug · 8pm (doors 7:30) — Fri has an artist Q&A

Audium, 1616 Bush St, Lower Nob Hill San Francisco

176 speakers, complete darkness, no stage and nothing to look at. collier moves hundreds of field recordings through the room — Candomblé devotees, a second line, bomba, ring shouts, water drumming, Hoodoo elders — to trace Maafa migration routes across the diaspora. Saturday closes the run. Limited pay-what-you-can at the door, first come.

Literary & Ideas

Five days of a DIY intellectual festival in Oakland, Ezra Klein interviewing Annie Lowrey, and a novelist back after twenty-eight years.

TOP PICK✦ Annual, five days

Bathers Library Summer Symposium (2nd annual)

Wed Aug 26 6pm – Sun Aug 30 8pm

Bathers Library, 2310 Telegraph Ave, Uptown Oakland + satellite venues East Bay

The whole Oakland small-press and artist-run scene thinking out loud for five days: a brief history of reverb, culinary taboos from pork to sago grubs, Gertrude Stein and the poetics of nonsense, the poetry and philosophy of Oakland code enforcement, Stanford's Adrian Daub reading from What Tech Calls Governing. Ends Sunday with a sauna. Nobody turned away for lack of funds.

Notes, caveats and what was left out

Times were verified on each venue's own event page wherever one exists, in preference to aggregator grids. A few things still need a check before you commit:

  • Audium's closing date. The venue's own site contradicts itself (one section says Aug 27, the calendar and City Box Office say the run goes to Aug 29). Bay Improviser lists all three nights. Treat Sat Aug 29 as the closer but confirm at the box office.
  • BATS Cave Match Maestro (Sat). Eventbrite renders the curtain time only at checkout; the venue's Saturday mainstage slot is usually 8pm.
  • The Time Masters at the Roxie — the calendar and the film page disagree on Wed Aug 26 vs Thu Aug 27.
  • Central Works' The Prince alternates Part 1 and Part 2 and publishes the rotation only as an image; ring 510.558.1381. All performances are currently fully reserved with a waitlist.
  • Bridge Live Arts' Love Language — Dancers' Group lists 447 Minna, the presenter lists Studio 210 on Cesar Chavez. The presenter's page wins, but confirm.
  • Altarena's Fallen Angels — the show page says 7:30pm, the press release says 8pm.
  • Telescope nights are weather-dependent. The forecast is clear Thu–Sat, but Chabot closes the deck above 90% humidity and Foothill closes on cloud. Both have day-of hotlines.
  • Sold out as of building this: BAMPFA's Elevator to the Gallows and Princess Kaguya, the Commonwealth Club's Odyssey talk, CHM Live in person, and most of the Marsh Berkeley festival. Returns do appear.

Deliberately left out: EDM and DJ club nights, arena and amphitheatre concerts (Bonnie Raitt, Courtney Barnett, Nas, T.I., Jill Scott all played this week), sports, bar crawls, networking mixers and sales expos — including the Pokémon World Championships at Moscone. LGBTQ- and Pride-specific programming was deprioritised for this run per a standing instruction; a handful of items that would otherwise have ranked highly — BAMPFA's Tongues Untied, KALW's Solidarity Cinema, ODC's Daisy-Chain<><><>Star-Connection world premiere — were held back on that basis rather than on merit.

One good thing that isn't listed: Niles Essanay Silent Film Museum is screening Eisenstein's October (1928) on a 16mm print with live music on Sat Aug 29 at 7:30pm in Fremont. It is arguably the rarest screening of the week, but the museum's site is a JavaScript shell that no reader can open, so there is no event page to link and it has been left out of the cards rather than published without a working link.

Sources that could not be read this week: Visit Oakland's arts sub-feed (its API rejects unauthenticated calls), the Oakland Review of Books weekly calendar, SF Station's category calendars (403), and Grace Cathedral's own events list — the Sacred Voices and Fontana entries were confirmed through other routes. CounterPulse, SF Ballet, SF Symphony, SF Opera, SF Performances, Cal Performances, Stanford Live, Berkeley Rep, A.C.T., Magic Theatre and SFJAZZ Center are all genuinely dark this week; their seasons start in September.
